verdict: Netflix's revenue rose 16% to $12.2B, and a one-off $2.8B Warner Bros. termination fee lifted net income to $5.3B — while the underlying streaming business earned a 32% operating margin.

kpis.note: vs a year ago; +14% at constant currency

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.66 a year ago — boosted by a one-off fee

segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — subscription streaming, plus the fast-growing ads business.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region, growing faster than North America this quarter (12% at constant currency).

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Cheaper plans are pulling in new households — up 19% as reported, 18% at constant currency.

segments.name: Asia-Pacific
segments.note: The fastest-growing region this quarter — mobile-first plans in price-sensitive markets.

takeaways.title: A one-off fee flattered everything
takeaways.text: Netflix collected a $2.8B termination fee after its Warner Bros. transaction was called off. It is the main reason EPS of $1.23 came in far above Netflix's own $0.76 forecast — and it will not repeat.

takeaways.title: The core business still grew
takeaways.text: Even before the fee, operating income rose 18% YoY to $4.0B at a 32.3% margin — the streaming engine itself had a strong quarter.

takeaways.title: Every region grew double digits
takeaways.text: Asia-Pacific grew fastest at +20%, Latin America +19%, EMEA +17% and UCAN +14% — broad growth, not one market carrying the quarter.

oneTimers: A $2.8B termination fee from the Warner Bros. transaction sits inside 'interest and other income' ($2,852M in total). It is one-off cash: operating cash flow of $5.3B and free cash flow of $5.1B both include it, and Netflix raised its full-year free-cash-flow expectation to about $12.5B largely because of it.
otherDetail: A $2.8B termination fee from the Warner Bros. transaction, inside total interest and other income of $2,852M, less $262M of interest expense on Netflix's debt — a net +$2,590M below operating profit.
